title: Quote to delivery day: how Dubai catering bookings are confirmed
body_markdown:
Instead of chasing menus, messages and delivery details separately, organise the catering booking process in Dubai around one written event brief, an agreed quotation and a final delivery plan. Before treating a booking as confirmed, ask the caterer to identify the acceptance and payment requirements, then record exactly who is responsible for food, setup, service and collection.


**TL;DR**

- For the catering booking process Dubai hosts need, agree the brief, quotation, confirmation requirements and delivery plan in writing.
- myCHEF provides catering for households and businesses; request an event-specific proposal rather than assuming standard inclusions.
- Separate arrival, setup and serving times so the delivery plan matches your event.
- After any change, request a revised summary covering the menu, guest count, staffing and responsibilities.


For a tailored proposal, use the [myCHEF catering enquiry form](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) to share your event details and request the relevant service. This guide explains how to move from that enquiry to a clear handover, without assuming that every caterer uses the same booking terms.

## Why a quotation is not the whole booking

A menu describes the food. A complete booking also needs to explain how that food reaches your guests, what happens on site and which responsibilities remain with you.

**myCHEF catering is suited to Dubai households and businesses seeking food service for a specific event.** Its suitability for your occasion depends on the agreed menu, service scope and practical arrangements, not the menu alone.

Keep the quotation and the operational plan together. If delivery instructions sit in a separate conversation that nobody has acknowledged, they are not a reliable handover plan.

## Before you start

Prepare these materials before requesting or accepting a proposal:

- **An event brief:** date, location, expected guest count, occasion, preferred serving time and the format you want. Mark estimates clearly rather than presenting them as final numbers.
- **Decision-making access:** identify who approves the menu and quotation, who arranges payment, and who can confirm venue access. For a business event, check whether internal purchasing approval is needed.
- **Venue information:** confirm loading access, parking instructions, lift arrangements and any kitchen or preparation space. The easily missed detail is whether the team can enter early enough to complete the agreed setup.

Do not assume the event organiser controls every part of the venue. Ask the building or venue contact to verify arrangements before you include them in the brief.

## Event brief and service format

### Turn your enquiry into a working brief

1. **State the occasion and location.** Give the full venue details and explain whether the event is at a home, office or another location. Add the on-site contact separately if that person is not the person booking.
2. **Describe the guest count.** Distinguish confirmed guests from an estimate. Explain whether children, suppliers or event staff need food rather than leaving the caterer to infer this.
3. **Separate the timings.** Record the requested arrival time, setup completion time and serving time. These are 3 different milestones, even if your event schedule initially shows only a start time.
4. **Describe the food requirements.** List preferred dishes or cuisines, dietary requirements, allergies and any ingredients you want excluded. Ask the caterer to confirm what can be accommodated.
5. **Name the service responsibilities.** Explain whether you want food handed over, a serving area prepared or staff present during the event. Ask which elements the caterer can include.

**Expected result:** you have a brief that another person can read without needing the original message thread to understand the event.

### Choose the format before comparing proposals

A quotation for food delivery is not directly comparable with one that includes setup and service. Use the following planning comparison to describe the scope you want; it does not represent a list of standard myCHEF packages.

| Service format | Best for | Main benefit | Main limitation | Confirm in the proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Food handover | Hosts managing their own serving arrangements | Keeps the caterer's on-site role focused on delivery | You retain responsibility for arranging and serving the food | Packaging, handover instructions and equipment responsibilities |
| Delivery and setup | Events needing a prepared serving area | Gives setup a defined place in the plan | Setup does not establish that staff remain afterwards | Setup scope, table requirements and departure point |
| Staffed service | Hosts wanting an agreed team present during the event | Assigns service tasks to named roles | Requires more detailed staffing, access and finish-time arrangements | Roles, service duration, clearing and collection |

**Choose the service format by the work you want someone else to own.** A shorter quotation is not necessarily a simpler event if it leaves you arranging equipment, serving food and clearing the venue.

## Quotation review and written acceptance

### Check the scope before you approve it

1. **Match the proposal to the brief.** Check the date, venue, guest count and serving format first. Resolve any mismatch before discussing menu refinements.
2. **Read the menu as an event plan.** Confirm dish selections, how the food will be presented and which dietary alternatives are included. Ask how individual dietary meals will be identified at handover or service.
3. **Check staffing and equipment.** Ask who brings serving utensils, crockery, glassware, tables and any preparation equipment required for the agreed menu. Treat unanswered items as unresolved, not included.
4. **Separate inclusions from exclusions.** Ask whether transport, setup, service, clearing and equipment collection form part of the quotation. Request an explanation of any charges or taxes shown without copying them into your event brief from memory.
5. **Request the booking conditions.** Ask what constitutes acceptance, whether payment is required to confirm, and what terms apply to changes or cancellation. Read the actual proposal rather than relying on another event's arrangements.
6. **Obtain written acknowledgement.** After completing the stated requirements, ask for confirmation that the booking is accepted against the agreed version of the proposal.

**Expected result:** both sides can identify the same accepted scope and the requirements that have been completed.

The factors to clarify include menu complexity, guest count, staffing, equipment, transport and time on site. These belong in the proposal discussion; this guide does not establish standard charges or booking terms.

For myCHEF catering, request event-specific confirmation of every inclusion that matters to you. Do not assume that chef attendance, serving staff or clearing follows automatically from the word catering.

### Keep approval unambiguous

Use a short written acceptance that identifies the proposal version and event details. For example: please confirm acceptance of the attached proposal for the stated date, venue, guest count and service scope, subject to its listed booking requirements.

That wording is a communication aid, not a substitute for the caterer's agreement. If the reply changes a condition, resolve it before marking the booking complete in your own calendar.

## Delivery plan and event-day handover

### Build the practical schedule

1. **Verify the route into the venue.** Share the correct entrance, delivery point, parking instructions and relevant access contact. Ask the venue whether any registration or permission is required; do not assume a universal Dubai access rule.
2. **Confirm the working space.** Describe available surfaces, kitchen access and any equipment the caterer has requested. Send accurate photographs if they help explain the space, without promising facilities you have not checked.
3. **Agree the handover point.** Identify who receives the food or team and who checks the delivery against the agreed menu. Provide a reachable contact and a backup contact where practical.
4. **Confirm the event sequence.** Record when setup ends, when guests eat and when any agreed clearing or collection takes place. Keep speeches, presentations or other schedule constraints visible.
5. **Request handling instructions.** Ask the caterer for instructions relevant to the supplied food and serving format. Do not replace those instructions with generic reheating or storage advice.
6. **Circulate the final summary.** Send the agreed version to the organiser, caterer and relevant venue contact. Ask each person to acknowledge the parts they control.

**Expected result:** the people handling delivery, access and service know where to go, when to act and whom to contact.

Keep the sequence visible in your planning document: **Event brief**, **Accepted quotation**, **Access plan**, **Final handover**. Resolve dependencies in that order rather than trying to fix access while food is arriving.


![Four booking stages from the event brief to the final catering handover](https://media.get-ryze.ai/workspace-article-images-public/536f57bb-a920-4372-93ad-97940d746d5e/body-365ee878da56b482808525d11cca8c18.jpg)

*An agreed menu still needs an access plan and a named handover contact.*


### Check what arrives against what was agreed

At handover, compare the delivered items or service setup with the accepted summary. Raise a missing item or unclear instruction with the agreed contact immediately, while the team can address it.

For staffed events, confirm who can authorise operational changes on site. For food handover, make sure the receiving person has the instructions needed after the delivery team leaves.

## When the guest count or venue changes

Use a revision workflow whenever an approved detail changes. An extra message containing a new guest count should not become a second, competing event brief.

1. **Identify the change.** State the original detail, the replacement detail and whether anything else is affected.
2. **Ask for the consequences.** Request confirmation of menu, staffing, equipment, transport, timing and quotation changes where relevant.
3. **Check the booking terms.** Ask whether the change is accepted and what requirements apply. Do not assume acceptance because a message was received.
4. **Approve the revised summary.** Replace the superseded version and circulate the current plan to everyone affected.

**Expected result:** you retain 1 current event summary rather than several conflicting instructions.

A venue change deserves a fresh access check even when the menu stays identical. A different entrance, working area or serving location changes the practical plan.

## Troubleshooting booking and delivery problems

- **You have a quotation but no clear confirmation.** Ask which acceptance requirements remain outstanding and request an explicit booking status. A quotation alone does not tell you whether those requirements have been met.
- **The quotation and message thread show different menus.** Ask for a corrected proposal or consolidated summary. Avoid approving one document while expecting the team to follow another.
- **Delivery is scheduled for the serving time.** Ask the caterer to confirm whether setup is needed and revise arrival arrangements accordingly. Do not invent a setup allowance without checking the agreed service.
- **The venue cannot provide the assumed equipment.** Tell the caterer exactly what is missing and request a revised arrangement. Confirm any resulting scope changes before proceeding.
- **Dietary details arrive after approval.** Submit the new requirement promptly and ask what can be accommodated. Do not relabel a dish yourself or treat ingredient exclusion as confirmation of allergy suitability.

## Customize your workflow around the event

For an office event, add the facilities contact and internal approver to the relevant stages. For a home celebration, clarify which hosting tasks remain yours while the caterer works.

Keep the document short enough to use on the day. The accepted proposal can hold the detail; the event summary should make the menu version, timings, contacts and responsibilities easy to find.

## FAQ


**How does the catering booking process in Dubai work?**

Start with an event brief, review an itemised proposal, complete the caterer's stated acceptance requirements and agree the delivery plan. Request written confirmation identifying the accepted scope and event details.

**Does receiving a catering quote mean my booking is confirmed?**

No. Ask the caterer what confirms the booking and obtain acknowledgement after completing those requirements. A proposal does not by itself explain whether acceptance or payment conditions have been met.

**Do I need to pay a deposit to confirm catering?**

Follow the payment requirements stated in your event proposal. Ask the caterer to explain the confirmation conditions and applicable terms before you accept; this guide does not establish a standard deposit policy.

**What should I include in a catering enquiry?**

Include the event date, location, guest count, serving time and service required. Add dietary requirements, venue access information and the person responsible for approving the proposal.

**Can I change the guest count after confirming catering?**

Request the change and ask the caterer to confirm acceptance under the booking terms. Obtain a revised summary covering any effect on food, staffing, equipment and the quotation.

**Are serving staff and cleanup included in catering?**

Include serving staff and cleanup only when the proposal expressly confirms them. Ask which tasks are covered, when the team finishes and who handles any equipment collection.

**What should I send myCHEF for a catering proposal?**

Send myCHEF the date, Dubai location, guest count and catering service required. Include your preferred serving format, dietary requirements and practical venue details so the proposal can address your event.

- [Connecting office facilities management to lunch catering](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/how-to-connect-office-facilities-management-to-lunch-catering)

## One last check before you enquire

**The person receiving the delivery needs the final plan, not just the person paying for it.** Check that your on-site contact knows the agreed menu, arrival arrangements and handover responsibilities.

Send myCHEF your date, location, guest count and service required. Explain whether you need food handover, setup or staffed service, then ask for a proposal that makes the next confirmation step clear.
